setting_premise.name: Setting Premise
patterns: they call it {realm}, a place where {pressure} and {stake}

realm: a river kingdom of oath-bound clans
a highland realm of stair-forts and sworn herdsmen
a free city ruling a league of market towns
a frontier march of watching forts and thin fields
a reclaimed sorcerer-realm of broken towers
a forest principality of chartered woodwards
a coastal domain of salt-pans and tide-priests
a mountain vale kingdom that pays tribute in iron
pressure: the old roads are walking at night
the crown has three claimants and no clear heir
the temple's oracle has fallen silent
the border pacts are coming due
the dead no longer rest where they were buried
the harvest has failed three years running
the guilds have bought the courts outright
the wild clans have united under one banner
stake: a generation's peace hangs on who holds the pass
the right to rule waits for whoever can prove it
something sealed and forgotten is waiting to be found
every family's land grant can be lost or made good
the realm's soul is being bargained away one temple at a time
there is wealth enough to buy any loyalty that is for sale
the next harvest decides whether the villages rise or empty
the crown's favour is worth more than any coin

land: a drowned river valley of willow islands
a high moor of peat bog and standing stones
a coastal plain of dunes and salt marsh
a pine forest broken by clearings and burnt cabins
a chalk downland of dry valleys and sheep tracks
a mountain valley walled in by scree slopes
a lake country of reed beds and sunken causeways
an old frontier of hedged fields and empty forts
people: peat-cutters who keep the old fire festivals
herders who move their flocks by the stars
fisherfolk who will not sail on the turn of the moon
charcoal burners living in family camps
tenant farmers who remember every boundary stone
families of a garrison town, half soldiers and half innkeepers
weavers and dyers who work for distant markets
shrine-keepers and the pilgrims who winter there
mark: a bell tower that rings itself before storms
a road paved with stones too large for any cart
a standing stone that no one has been able to move
a market where no coin is allowed to change hands
a shrine that draws pilgrims from three rival realms
a lake that freezes a month before any other
a wall of black stone running through the fields
a festival that ends with every door left open

faction.name: Faction
patterns: {who} with one aim, to {wants}, and no scruple about {how}
to {wants}, {who} will go as far as {how}

who: the household of a disgraced noble house
a guild of carters and drovers
a band of forest outlaws with a written code
the heirs of a fallen sorcerer-realm
a council of village elders from the border hamlets
wants: recover a relic lost in the last war
break the guild's monopoly on iron
clear the roads of the monsters that prey on travellers
buy the loyalty of the frontier forts
keep the succession unsettled until they can choose the heir
open the sealed roads beyond the pass
how: marrying their children into better houses
spreading rumours in the market squares
hiring the desperate and paying them in land
holding the grain supply until the price is right
forging old charters and older seals
sheltering the realm's most wanted travellers

conflict.name: Conflict
patterns: {cause} has set {sides} against each other, and {flashpoint} may tip it into open war
because of {cause}, {sides} have armed themselves, and {flashpoint} is the point neither will yield
the quarrel began with {cause}: {sides} no longer speak, and everything now waits on {flashpoint}

cause: a levy no one agreed to
a well that failed in a dry summer
an old treaty read aloud for the first time in a century
a killing at a wedding feast
a shrine that two houses claim to have founded
a border stone moved in the night
a marriage promise broken after the dowry was paid
sides: the river towns and the hill clans
the old families and the new guilds
the free city and the lords of its hinterland
the herders and the farmers of the valley floor
the returning exiles and the tenants who took their land
the frontier garrisons and the capital's officers
two branches of the same ruling house
flashpoint: control of the ferry at the river crossing
the right to name the next temple warden
a grain shipment due at the end of the month
the wedding of two children promised years ago
the toll on the only bridge both sides need
the muster of the border levies
a debt called in on a single day

mystery.name: Mystery
patterns: the truth is that {secret}, and {evidence} is the only proof, but {danger} is already looking for it
what no one says aloud is that {secret}; {evidence} was meant to stay hidden, and {danger} has begun to ask questions
{evidence} is the only proof that {secret}, and {danger} would rather it vanished

secret: the founding oath was sworn to something that still listens
the ruling house has no claim to the throne it holds
the temple's holiest relic is a forgery made in living memory
the last war was started on purpose by the men who profited from it
the passes were never sealed by magic, only by an agreement no one has dared break
the old sorcerer-realm was not destroyed but moved
the foundlings left at the shrine are all of one bloodline
the plague that emptied the eastern villages never ended, only slept
evidence: a bundle of charters bearing the same date and different seals
a ledger with three pages cut out
a sealed letter in a dead clerk's handwriting
a coin struck with a face no one recognises
a map with the old road drawn straight through the hill
a key that fits a door no one can find
a list of names scraped off the temple wall
a stone tablet prised out of a collapsed well
danger: a rival antiquarian with a patron at court
an order of monks with a long memory
the family that has paid for silence for three generations
a mercenary captain who saw the same thing once before
a student who has read the wrong book
the widow of the man who wrote it

adventure_hook.name: Adventure Hook
patterns: {patron} hires the party to {goal}, but {obstacle} stands in the way, and {twist}
{patron} needs the party to {goal} before {obstacle} can stop them, and {twist}
a job from {patron}: {goal}, while {obstacle} closes in, and {twist}

patron: a merchant with a warehouse full of unsold wool
a village headman with a missing child
a minor noble with too many debts
a retired soldier who wants one thing done properly
a scholar too frail to travel alone
a guild factor with a sealed commission
the heir to a house no one will name aloud
goal: escort a witness to the capital
clear a road of its monster
deliver a sealed letter and ask no questions
bring back proof that a ruin is empty
escort a bride to a marriage neither family wants
recover a debt from a village that has nothing
obstacle: a rival company already on the road
the local magistrate, who wants the credit
a beast that hunts the road by night
the guild that controls the only road north
a bounty hunter with a grudge against one of the party
the temple that calls the whole business heresy
a rival heir with better advocates
the outlaw company that holds the only bridge
twist: the patron is not who they claim to be
the rival is acting on the same orders
one of the party has been here before
the job was arranged to lure the party away from somewhere else
someone has been paid to make sure the party fails
the whole job is a test rather than a task
the reward was never the patron's to offer
a second patron has a different commission
